target_customer: Pharma partners (licensing) and eventually patients with cancer, autoimmune disease and infections
problem: Delivering genetic medicines and cytotoxic payloads precisely to target cells is hard; the company wants to reuse the immune system's own attack particles as a programmable delivery vehicle.
business_model: Biotech platform; drug candidates plus partnership and licensing
product_category: Programmable immune-derived therapeutic delivery (supramolecular attack particles)

founders.name: Ashwin Nandakumar
founders.background_notes: Experience setting up oncology clinical trials and in oncology startups (YC page).

founders.name: Ashwin Jainarayanan
education: University of Oxford, DPhil Interdisciplinary Bioscience (Clarendon Scholar)
founders.background_notes: Synthetic immunologist with research on immune-cell-derived attack particles.

competitors.name: Evox Therapeutics
competitors.what: Engineered exosomes for CNS and rare disease delivery (DeliverEX)
competitors.traction_then: Lilly collaboration for up to five CNS exosome therapeutics; acquired Codiak's engEx-AAV platform in June 2023

competitors.name: Codiak BioSciences
competitors.what: Engineered exosome therapeutics; exoSTING reached a Phase I/II trial in 2021
competitors.traction_then: assets later sold or stranded (summary source of low quality)

technical_complexity.rationale: Isolating and reprogramming a newly described immune structure (attack particles, discovered at Oxford in 2020) is research-grade and needs wet-lab and manufacturing breakthroughs.

defensibility.rationale: Built on the discovering lab's work with Prof. Michael Dustin as co-founder; deep science and likely IP, though no patents were verified.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or copy found as of the sources; nobody else was found commercializing attack particles.

market_need_then: Delivery is the main bottleneck for genetic medicines and in vivo cell therapy; investor interest in in vivo CAR-T was high (Capstan $102M Series A led by Pfizer Ventures reported in the search results).

branding.domain_note: Uses granzabio.com; acquisition history not found.

identity.visual_style: Minimal single-page site built by Tonik

brand_strength.rationale: Early-stage biotech brand with a minimal site and no press about the brand itself; the name is plausibly drawn from granzymes but no source says so.

outcome_analysis: Granza Bio was founded in 2024 around the Oxford discovery of supramolecular attack particles, joined YC in Winter 2024 and closed a $7.14M seed led by Felicis and Refactor in July 2024. No later round, partnership, acquisition or shutdown was found, so it remains an early preclinical company whose outcome depends on scientific results not yet public.
notes: CB Insights snippet lists $7.64M across four rounds and founding year 2023; unverified and not recorded. Prof. Michael Dustin is described as co-founder by Oxford BioEscalator coverage but is not a YC-listed founder. Competitors are adjacent exosome players from undated or 2023 sources; they are loosely dated and the fit is approximate. Name origin not stated by any source.
